Discussed three prioritized joint opportunities, technical fit and benchmarking needs, potential procurement/timing risks, and proposed co-sell revenue split. Agreed next steps include Redwood sharing updated GTM deck and benchmarks, Asteria providing account targets, and scheduling an exec briefing to lock joint commitments.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Asteria Channel Lead), Mark Dawson (Asteria Sales Director), Sofia Ruiz (Asteria Solution Architect)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate you making time. Quick agenda — run through the joint pipeline, call out blockers, talk technical benchmark asks, and agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yep that works for us, thanks Maya. Mark and Sofia are on too, so we can go deal by deal.
[00:20] Mark Dawson: Hi all, hey Liam.
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: Hey Mark, hey Priya, hey Sofia. Quick note I might share screen later for the perf notes.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Cool, first up Opportunity A — healthcare customer, pre-sales stage, expected ramp Q1. Priya you said this was highest priority?
[00:38] Priya Patel: Yeah it's top prioritized. They're in digital intake workflows, heavy PII concerns. Procurement wants VPC or dedicated environment plus SOC2 evidence.
[00:48] Sofia Ruiz: Technical: they need on-prem or private deployment because of data residency and KMS. We looked at Redwood Private, but need latency targets sub-200ms for LLM responses; also model determinism is important.
[00:59] Liam O'Connor: Right, for sub-200ms we're looking at dedicated pool with optimized batching and KV cache. I flagged a couple of model variants we think fit. The tradeoff will be cost — quantization helps but may affect some output quality.
[01:15] Mark Dawson: On the commercial side, procurement said budget likely for dedicated but they need a clear SLA and audit logs. Can Redwood provide that in a PoC?
[01:24] Maya Chen: Yes we can offer a short-term Dedicated pilot and share SOC2 docs; need to coordinate with Product for SLA specifics. We'll send the standard security pack after the call.
[01:33] Priya Patel: Great, please include notes on KMS and HSM integration.
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: Noted — I'll include HSM/KMS integration notes and expected latency ranges per model.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Next, Opportunity B — large retail client, expected close in 6-8 weeks, RFP timeline tight.
[01:46] Mark Dawson: This one is tricky because the client is comparing to Anthropic and Vertex AI, pricing is sensitive. We need a crisp value prop on latency and cost per session.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: For retail we typically recommend Redwood Hosted for speed to value, or Dedicated if they want predictable throughput. For cost-sensitive workloads we can show batching and caching savings; I'll run a cost-per-1000-requests estimate with the customer's expected query distribution.
[02:12] Priya Patel: Could you also include an example prompt set? They want to see hallucination mitigation and relevance metrics.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: Sure — we'll include an eval run with top prompts and show quality/regression metrics.
[02:24] Maya Chen: Big picture on co-sell split — Asteria asked for a standard 60/40 split in favor of Asteria on introduced ARR, we proposed 70/30 in Redwood's favor on executive-involved deals. We need to reconcile and agree what qualifies as an introduced vs co-sourced deal.
[02:40] Priya Patel: Right, for channel-sourced leads we push for 60/40, for joint-account exec engagement we accept 65/35. We're open to finalizing by exec sync.
[02:48] Mark Dawson: Also need clarity on marketing funds and lead registration process.
[02:52] Maya Chen: I'll put a GTM doc together with lead registration flow and proposed MDF.
[02:57] Sofia Ruiz: On the tech side, for the retail proof we'll need a small sample dataset to run the benchmark — can Redwood run a blind perf test if we provide tokenized samples?
[03:06] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can run a blind perf test in a sandboxed environment. Need to confirm data obfuscation and whether PII is present. If it's real PII, we need a private environment.
[03:16] Priya Patel: We can provide synthetic but realistic samples for the benchmark, should be fine.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Great. Moving to Opportunity C — fintech prospect, longer sales cycle, big upside but heavy compliance (ISO, PCI considerations).
[03:29] Mark Dawson: They will want encryption at rest, HSM for keys, and detailed audit trails. Any showstoppers?
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: No showstoppers but for PCI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with a strong KMS/HSM integration. We should map their controls to our SOC2 report as a baseline.
[03:46] Priya Patel: Timing is a concern — procurement could take 2-3 months after contract. That delays revenue recognition. How do you propose we handle pipeline coverage?
[03:54] Maya Chen: We should mark it as commit with contingent close in CRM; propose a phased rollout — pilot first quarter, full deployment in next. We'll adjust ACV recognition expectations.
[04:06] Mark Dawson: Sounds reasonable.
[04:10] [04:10] Maya Chen: (laughs) Sorry timestamp hiccup — moving on.
[04:15] Liam O'Connor: Quick tech note: for the healthcare deal, if we can get a 1k token average prompt distribution, latency numbers look realistic. If they do 4k tokens, the numbers change a lot.
[04:27] Sofia Ruiz: Understood, I'll confirm typical prompt sizes.
[04:31] Priya Patel: What about integration support? Asteria wants to know if Redwood will co-assign an SE for the initial onboarding.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Yes, we typically include an onboarding SE for the pilot; that's already part of the Dedicated pilot offer. We'll detail SE hours in the pilot scope doc.
[04:46] Mark Dawson: Procurement also asked about exit clauses and IP — they want reassurance that training data isn't shared.
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: Redwood doesn't retain customer data beyond configured retention, and we have options for customer-managed keys. I'll include data retention and IP language references from our standard terms.
[05:04] Priya Patel: Please send the standard terms excerpt. That will speed procurement.
[05:08] Maya Chen: Will do.
[05:10] [05:10] Liam O'Connor: I pulled up a rough benchmark spreadsheet. (screen share) sorry transcription might garble some numbers — but I have baseline latencies for the model family A vs B on gpus, and cost-per-token estimates with quantization profiles.
[05:24] Mark Dawson: Can you highlight the sweet spot for retail? We need the best cost/latency point.
[05:29] Liam O'Connor: For retail, model B with int8 quant and batching looks like the best compromise — ~180-250ms median P95 and 30% cost savings vs fp16. But quality delta is small on intent classification tasks.
[05:44] Priya Patel: Good. Can we package that into a one-pager? The customer wants short executive docs.
[05:50] Maya Chen: We'll do a GTM one-pager and include those benchmark numbers.
[05:54] Sofia Ruiz: Also include recommended config for caching and prefix caching — that'll reduce token usage for repetitive flows.
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: Yep — caching recommendations and expected hit rates.
[06:07] Mark Dawson: Any legal or procurement red flags we should surface?
[06:10] Maya Chen: Main ones: procurement timeline, SSO/SAML requirements, audit logs retention length, and KMS language. We'll propose standard positions but leave room for negotiation.
[06:20] Priya Patel: On partner motions, Asteria would like a co-branded case study after a successful pilot. We should plan for that early.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll include a joint case study template in the GTM package.
[06:32] [06:32] Mark Dawson: Quick question — competitors, are there specific technical differentiators vs Anthropic we should emphasize?
[06:39] Liam O'Connor: Two things: predictable inference economics via Dedicated and caching, and seamless parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so customers don't rework integrations as they move from pilot to prod. Those are things Anthropic/Vertex don't always call out.
[06:56] Priya Patel: Good points.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Let's go deal-by-deal ask list so we leave with clear owners. Opportunity A (healthcare): Asteria to confirm prompt sizes and provide synthetic samples (Priya). Redwood to send Dedicated pilot scope + SOC2 + KMS notes (Maya/Liam). Opportunity B (retail): Asteria to get RFP details to Redwood by EOW (Mark). Redwood to run retail eval and send one-pager and benchmark (Liam). Opportunity C (fintech): Asteria to initiate procurement pre-reads, Redwood to map controls to SOC2 and provide phased rollout plan.
[07:34] Priya Patel: Confirming deadlines — we can get samples to you by 2026-10-11. RFP for retail by 2026-10-09.
[07:43] Maya Chen: Perfect.
[07:45] [07:45] (brief cross-talk)
[07:48] Mark Dawson: On comp splits, we should prep a few scenarios to present to our execs — 60/40, 65/35, and a revenue share with MDF in the middle.
[07:59] Maya Chen: We'll draft scenarios and send them over.
[08:03] Priya Patel: One operational ask — do you have a partner portal or shared pipeline view? That helps us keep joint opps aligned.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We can give you partner access to a shared CRM view and also send weekly pipeline reports. We'll coordinate on granularity.
[08:18] Sofia Ruiz: For benchmarks, is it possible to run an A/B between Hosted (fast to start) and Dedicated (for final perf)?
[08:25] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can run an A/B; we'll need the same prompt/sample set for both and then compare cost/latency/quality.
[08:33] Mark Dawson: Any blockers to scheduling the exec sync Oct 20?
[08:37] Priya Patel: Should be fine, I'll confirm availability after this call.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Great. Last quick thing: do we want to involve the legal teams now or wait till pilot scope is accepted?
[08:49] Mark Dawson: Procurement prefers early sightline on terms; maybe a redline-ready excerpt.
[08:53] Maya Chen: We'll share standard terms excerpt as requested.
[08:57] [08:57] (wrap-up)
[09:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Recap: Redwood to send GTM deck, pilot scope, SOC2 and KMS notes; SE to run benchmarks; Asteria to send samples, RFP details and account targets; coordinate exec sync for Oct 20.
[09:18] Priya Patel: Thanks Maya, appreciate it.
[09:20] Mark Dawson: Thanks team.
[09:22] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the spreadsheet.
[09:25] Sofia Ruiz: Bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-attributions and timestamps—recording auto-transcript had some garbled numbers during the screen share. Links shared during call: https://redwood.ai/gTM-deck (note: placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (internal link), joint GTM template (placeholder).
